name: f7-delivery-stories-v1
idea_origin: trace diagnosis of the 38 cloud Haiku digests (lab/reports/cloud-run-diagnostics/block3-generation.md, table 4: stats lost between the last quarterly phase and the review)
hypothesis: Output or Network lost in the story events between the last quarterly phase and a review cannot be restored by Energy before that review, and the loss costs the grade: at Level 1-2 a B or promotion followed 14 of 60 reviews with such a loss against 34 of 66 without (leader digests: 3 of 6 reviews had one, including both C reviews at Level 2 in e373478a-04). The losing story options share a visible pattern (delays, side duties, other people's processes, pauses), the gaining ones another (finishing, fixing or showing your own work), and Haiku's default choice in an event is the same across policies, so a rule that switches its preference while Output or Network is below its recent high will cut these losses and raise the share of good reviews without adding hidden risk.
change: story-decisions: new rule 2 'While Output or Network is below its recent high, prefer finishing, fixing or showing your own work, or settling things directly with the people involved, over side duties, other people's processes or delays, unless delivering would hide a problem or Health is low.' Parent rules 2-3 become 3-4 unchanged. risk-review and quarterly-planning strategy lines unchanged. Shared trims in all three block-3 children (no strategy change): shorter front-matter descriptions with the same 'Use ...' triggers; the redundant line 'Do this before every decision.' removed; the check_latest_logs line shortened to the context-reset case; quarterly step 4 ('Keep the same rules all run; near the end, avoid new risks.') removed because 'near the end' is a run-phase trigger the block-3 brief forbids. Manifest instruction kept identical to the parent's routing sentence (the generic template has an empty instruction; keeping it avoids a routing confound). 372 words by wc -w (parent 398).
predicted_behaviour: When Output or Network has fallen, notes say so and pick the option that finishes, fixes or shows the agent's own work or settles things with the people involved; options that postpone, pause or add side duties are taken only with a stated hidden-problem or low-Health reason. Reviews below Level 3 with a post-quarter loss of Output or Network: at most 1 in 3 (parent 3 of 6; population 60 of 126). B or promotion at 2/3 or more of reviews below Level 3 (parent 4 of 6). Months with the HR remark at 'risks have piled up' or worse not above the parent's level; no trust crisis; mean quantitative_score at or above the parent's raw mean (59.7).
refutation: On a 4-run Haiku screen against f7-three-skills-v1: refuted if post-quarter losses fall below the parent's share but good reviews (B or promotion) below Level 3 do not rise (wrong mechanism), or if risk warnings at 'piled up' or worse, blow-ups or a trust crisis rise above the parent's (the hidden-problem exception fails), or if mean quantitative_score is below the parent's by more than the decision margin. Uninformative if the loss share does not fall (Haiku ignores the rule).
notes: Story-side lever only; the parent's size-based risk marking is kept so this child separates from f7-trend-marking-v1 (marking by trend, no new story preference). Event text was used for diagnosis only: the rule names generic option types, no event. Diagnosis caveat: within an event Haiku nearly always takes the same option across policies, so the digests cannot estimate the option effect directly; the screen is the first test. Lint: see block3-generation.md.
